Ensuring a reliable blood supply during a pandemic in a Caribbean setting: The Curaçao experience.
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: National blood systems require a resilient mechanism for ensuring safe blood supply during pandemics. For small island developing states (SIDS) additional specific challenges exist not normally addressed in guidelines and the literature. Here we describe the model used by the Caribbean island of Curaçao for pandemic preparedness during the COVID-19 pandemic. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Key measures taken by the Red Cross Blood bank Foundation Curaçao during the COVID-19 pandemic were examined. National blood program data were analyzed retrospectively. RESULTS: For pandemic preparedness, critical main processes were adapted during the COVID-19 pandemic. These included individual donor time-scheduled phlebotomy sessions and government-authorized lockdown travel permits. Work procedures focusing on the prevention of simultaneous presence of personnel during shifts were introduced. Donor information was provided during governmental public health briefings. Patient blood management programs were adopted according to international recommendations in consultation with the blood bank. During the COVID-19 pandemic, characterized by four severe outbreaks over 2 years, donor availability and donations were maintained with sufficient labile blood product supply to all hospitals served. CONCLUSION: For SIDS, effective small-scale implementation of international recommendations on pandemics remains challenging. The national blood program preparedness model of Curaçao proved to be successful during the COVID-19 pandemic, ensuring uninterrupted donor participation and sufficient labile blood product availability. Key success factors of the model were a voluntary, non-remunerated, repetitive donor program, a central blood collection facility, acknowledgement of the blood bank as important in the public health pandemic response, and effective communication with donors, hospitals, and health authorities.

Structural basis for the broad-spectrum inhibition of the coronavirus main protease by Zevotrelvir.
Beta-coronaviruses have caused three major coronavirus outbreaks, underscoring the urgent need for broad-spectrum antivirals. The coronavirus main protease (Mpro) is an ideal drug target due to its high conservation and absence of human homologs. Zevotrelvir (EDP-235) is an oral Mpro inhibitor with broad-spectrum activity against betacoronaviruses, but its molecular mechanism remains unclear. Here, we systematically evaluated Zevotrelvir against SARS-CoV-2 Mpro and its mutants (G15S, M49I, K90R, S144A), as well as SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV Mpro, using enzyme activity assays, crystallography, and molecular dynamics simulations. Zevotrelvir potently inhibited SARS-CoV-2 Mpro (IC50 = 23 nM) and maintained micromolar activity against mutants and other coronaviruses. Structural analysis revealed that Zevotrelvir forms a conserved covalent bond with the catalytic C145 (C148 in MERS-CoV) via its nitrile warhead, while its spirolactam and trifluoroindole groups occupy the S1', S1, S2, and S4 subsites through an E166-centered hydrogen bond network and hydrophobic interactions. Notably, conformational asymmetry was observed within the Mpro dimer, with the trifluoroindole moiety rotating ~80° in protomer B. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed complex stability and identified the key hydrogen bonds. This study elucidates the molecular basis of Zevotrelvir's broad-spectrum inhibition, informing its clinical development and next-generation drug design.

Barriers and Enablers to Asynchronous Secure Messaging Use in Hospital-Based Ambulatory Specialty Clinics in Ontario, Canada: Convergent Mixed Methods Study.
BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the adoption of virtual care, including patient-to-provider asynchronous secure messaging (ASM). However, while ASM offers access and convenience, the surge in message volume can increase physician workload and contribute to burnout. Furthermore, it has raised additional concerns about message appropriateness, medicolegal liability, and sustainability of this communication virtual care modality. OBJECTIVE: This study aims to explore the experience with ASM in Ontario in specialty ambulatory care to inform current practice support strategies. We sought to characterize messaging usage quantitatively while also exploring experience with messaging, contextual barriers, and facilitators qualitatively. METHODS: We used a convergent mixed methods design, analyzing aggregated electronic health record (EHR) usage and qualitative interview data. The study was conducted at a large ambulatory care hospital in Ontario, Canada, across four high-messaging specialty clinics: mental health, rheumatology, dermatology, and surgery. Quantitative data (October 2019 to Octtober 2022) included message volumes, response patterns, and timing. Semistructured interviews with physicians, nurses, administrative staff, and patients (n=19), conducted in 2022 explored ASM workflows, barriers, and facilitators. Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively, stratified by clinic. Qualitative data were analyzed using thematic analysis, informed by an interpretative phenomenological orientation. Findings from the two strands were then compared to identify areas of convergence and divergence. RESULTS: Message volumes surged post pandemic, particularly in mental health, ranging from about 6000 in surgery, rheumatology, and dermatology to close to 13,000 messages in mental health across the study period. Message rate per patient per month was 0.6 (SD 0.2; mental health), 0.5 (SD 0.2; rheumatology), 0.2 (SD 0.2; dermatology), and 0.2 (SD 0.1; surgery). Physicians averaged 12.6 (SD 8.0) messages/month (rheumatology) and 7.6 (SD 4.4) messages/month (mental health) in clinics without nursing support. Nurses handled 27.4 (SD 11.6) messages/month (surgery) and 19.2 (SD 14.1) messages/month (dermatology). Three percent (1263/38,370) to 10% (3619/36,022) of provider messages were sent outside regular hours. The majority of conversations (2156/6859, 46% to 6913/13,615, 62%) had only a single reply. Physicians reported challenging experiences due to increased workload, lack of compensation, and poor integration into local clinical workflows. High patient-to-physician ratios and limited nursing support for message triage were associated with a poor messaging experience. Patients and administrative staff valued messaging for its convenience, accessibility, and efficiency. A key finding was insufficient engagement across all user groups in decisions about messaging implementation. CONCLUSIONS: The study highlights a disconnect between the high perceived value of ASM for patients and administrative staff and the challenging experiences of physicians. Successful implementation requires thoughtful integration into care models, clear guidelines for appropriate use, and proper triage and "channel management" to guide patients to appropriate modalities. Future research should explore triaging algorithms as part of a digital front door, specialty-specific variations, and the crucial role of nursing staff in message channel management.

Public Awareness, Attitudes, and Practices Toward Digital Health Surveillance in Malawi: Cross-Sectional Study.
BACKGROUND: Digital surveillance systems are increasingly recognized as essential tools for enhancing early outbreak detection, reporting, and response, especially in low-resource settings. The COVID-19 pandemic unveiled the critical role of digital health surveillance systems in timely detection, monitoring, and responses to public health threats. However, successful implementation depends on public awareness, acceptance, and willingness to participate. Limited evidence exists on how the public perceives and interacts with digital surveillance in Malawi. OBJECTIVE: The aim of the study was to assess the awareness, attitudes, and practices of adult Malawians toward digital surveillance during pandemics and epidemics. METHODS: A cross-sectional quantitative study design was used. Data were collected in 10 selected districts (Chitipa, Mzimba South, Kasungu, Lilongwe, Salima, Balaka, Thyolo, Phalombe, Blantyre, and Chikwawa) of Malawi that had high and low levels of cholera and COVID-19 disease burden. The survey recruited 1174 participants who were 18 years or older at the time of data collection. Descriptive statistics were computed using R statistical software. Ethical approval was obtained from the National Health Sciences Research Committee prior to data collection. RESULTS: A total of 1174 participants were surveyed, 65% (n=768) were female, and the mean age was 36.9 (SD 14.26) years. Only 59% (n=697) demonstrated awareness of digital surveillance systems, though 51% (n=603) had smartphones and 41% (n=477) used mobile phones. A positive attitude was observed in 89% (n=1044) of respondents, with most believing digital reporting could improve outbreak control, and 80% (n=939) were confident in privacy and data security. Practices related to digital reporting were low, with only 18% (n=211) having ever reported health symptoms through any digital platform. CONCLUSIONS: Enhancing digital health surveillance literacy, promoting inclusivity, and ensuring accountability will improve readiness for future pandemics through digital surveillance systems. Hence, there is a need for nationwide community sensitization programs to raise awareness about the benefits of digital health surveillance.

Pregnancy and Influenza Vaccination Behavior in the United States.
Objectives. To estimate the influence of pregnancy on influenza vaccination before, during, and after pregnancy across the 2017-2018 to 2021-2022 influenza seasons in the United States. Methods. Using Optum's de-identified Clinformatics Data Mart Database, we conducted a retrospective cohort study examining influenza vaccination uptake among pregnant individuals before, during, and after their pregnancies. We used difference-in-differences analyses to assess changes in the pregnancy and postpregnancy effects across influenza seasons. Results. Influenza vaccination uptake was highest during pregnancy (44.6%), compared with the before- (27.6%) and after-pregnancy cohorts (30.1%). Pregnant individuals had more than twice the odds of vaccination during pregnancy compared with before pregnancy (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 2.3; 95% confidence interval [CI] = 2.26, 2.33). The postpregnancy effect was modest (AOR = 1.17; 95% CI = 1.15, 1.19). Both pregnancy and postpregnancy effects decreased after the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic. Conclusions. Influenza vaccination uptake was higher during pregnancy but decreased after delivery in the United States. Pregnancy is a key opportunity to promote immunization through prenatal care. Strengthening provider engagement and extending vaccine recommendations into the postpregnancy period may help sustain vaccination uptake. (Am J Public Health. Published online ahead of print October 22, 2026:e1-e10. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308636).

The impacts of host community composition, clustering and vector host choice on zoonotic mosquito-borne virus transmission.
Zoonotic mosquito-borne viruses, including West Nile, Rift Valley fever and Japanese encephalitis viruses, present a substantial public health burden in some countries, with transmission involving complex interactions between multiple vector and host species, making control difficult. While host community composition is known to affect transmission, the role of host community structure coupled with mosquito aggregation behaviour remains poorly understood. Motivated by furthering understanding of potential Japanese encephalitis virus transmission routes and persistence in contexts where cattle - dead-end hosts - are dominant in the community, we developed a patch model in which host distributions and the resulting mosquito biting allocation among patches are fixed within each simulation. This framework represents mosquito host-seeking across two scales: long-range aggregation toward host-dense patches and short-range host species choice determined by local host availability and innate vector preference. Using this model, assuming that vectors prefer dead-end hosts (choosing them 90% of the time if given an equal choice of other hosts), we explored the potential effect of host clustering, patch fragmentation, and the strength of mosquito aggregation on the basic reproduction number. Our results show that identical host communities can yield very different transmission outcomes depending on how they are distributed and the level of mosquito aggregation. Under circumstances where dead-end hosts are preferred by vectors, if competent hosts are clustered and mosquitoes aggregate strongly, transmission may be amplified compared with uniformly distributed hosts and vectors. If dead-end hosts are clustered, transmission may be diluted as mosquitoes aggregate in patches where dead-end hosts are dominant in the host community. Fragmentation effects are context-dependent: when competent hosts are clustered and mosquitoes aggregate, increasing patches increases transmission. When dead-end hosts are clustered, transmission decreases under strong mosquito aggregation with increasing number of patches. These findings highlight that variations in the local spatial context of host-vector interactions can lead to variations in disease risk. Locally-informed surveillance and targeted interventions may therefore be important in attempts to prevent outbreaks of zoonotic mosquito-borne viruses.

Imported chikungunya in French travelers returning from outbreak-affected regions.
BACKGROUND: Outbreaks of chikungunya disease are unpredictable, typically episodic, and explosive. In 2025, several such outbreaks were observed and a marked increase in imported cases of chikungunya to mainland France was reported. This study aimed to describe the rate of chikungunya in French travelers returning from La Réunion, Mayotte, Mauritius, Madagascar, Sri Lanka, and Cuba, all of which showed major chikungunya resurgences in 2025, and to assess the potential burden that CHIKV outbreaks-whether officially notified or not-can cause to travelers. METHODS: Publicly available data from Santé Publique France were used to extract the number of chikungunya cases, and International Air Transport Association data were used for information on the number of flight tickets to estimate traveler numbers. These data were used to derive monthly rates of imported cases of chikungunya to mainland France from January to December 2025. RESULTS: Trends in rates of chikungunya among travelers returning to mainland France from La Réunion and Mayotte closely mirrored the sharp and compact epidemic curves observed locally. Peak imported rates exceeded 1,800 cases/100,000 travelers (La Réunion [April]) and 400 cases/100,000 travelers (Mayotte [May]) and remained above 100 cases/100,000 travelers for March, April, May, and June (La Réunion) and April, May, and June (Mayotte). For Mauritius, Madagascar, Sri Lanka, and Cuba, estimated peak rates were 248, 338, 90, and 2,480 cases/100,000 travelers, respectively, although it was noted that some outbreaks were not officially notified or were reported late. CONCLUSIONS: Returning travelers to mainland France from regions facing a chikungunya outbreak in 2025 showed a substantial burden of infection and gave rise to local spread of disease, highlighting the importance of robust surveillance systems and timely outbreak notification.

Antagonism of PRDX1 and Japanese encephalitis virus via the autophagy pathway.
Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV) is a mosquito-borne zoonotic infectious agent and causes animal and human illness of the central nervous system. Japanese encephalitis virus inflicts severe harm, yet even with an approved vaccine, prevention and control remain daunting, and the molecular mechanism underlying the virus-host interplay remains incompletely understood. In this study, we found that the host peroxiredoxin 1 (PRDX1) protein inhibits JEV replication. PRDX1 targets nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) of JEV and mediates its degradation via the proteasome and autophagy pathways, thus inhibiting viral replication. By targeting TRAF6, an E3 ligase, the PRDX1 protein catalyzes the ubiquitination of NS1, leading to its recognition by NDP52, a cargo receptor, along with lysosomal degradation. We also found that the JEV NS3 protein can target and degrade PRDX1 to decrease the antiviral function of PRDX1, which is a tactic by which viruses confront the host. In conclusion, these findings showed that selective autophagy has dual functions in the host and JEV: it can degrade viral proteins to inhibit viral replication and host antiviral proteins to promote viral replication.IMPORTANCEJapanese encephalitis virus (JEV) is a flavivirus capable of inducing human encephalitis and dysgenesis in gestating sows. It has an extraordinary ability to hijack cellular systems and evade defenses, establishing infection and spreading it throughout the body to cause disease. During viral infection, the host initiates several antiviral responses and activates various host-restricted factors to resist viral invasion. In this study, we identified PRDX1 as a novel host restrictor that inhibits viral multiplication by binding to TRAF6 (an E3 ubiquitin ligase) and NDP52 (a cargo receptor) to degrade nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) of JEV. We also found that JEV infection can downregulate intracellular PRDX1 expression via nonstructural protein 3 (NS3), thus promoting viral replication. These results revealed that the virus-host interaction is a complex and dynamic process in which viruses restrict and compete with each other.

Immunologic and placental responses to the VSV-EBOV vaccine in a pregnant mouse model.
Ebola virus disease is a severe viral hemorrhagic illness with high maternal and perinatal mortality. Although the replication-competent vesicular stomatitis virus-based Ebola vaccine (VSV-EBOV) has been deployed successfully in outbreak settings, pregnant women were excluded from clinical trials, leaving critical safety gaps. To address this, we developed a murine model to assess pregnancy outcomes following VSV-EBOV exposure at different gestational stages. Pregnant C57BL/6 mice vaccinated at embryonic day 7 (E7), E10, or E15 mounted robust anti-Ebola virus (anti-EBOV) antibody responses comparable to those of non-pregnant controls and efficiently cleared the vaccine virus without evidence of vertical transmission. However, peri-implantation vaccination modestly increased fetal resorption and early postnatal mortality, accompanied by placental pathology characterized by vascular remodeling defects and inflammation. Later gestational vaccination had minimal impact on survival or offspring development. Mechanistic studies revealed that these adverse effects were mediated by type I interferon signaling rather than direct viral infection, as IFN-β-deficient mice exhibited normal pregnancy outcomes and blocking interferon receptor activity ameliorated placental pathology despite higher viral loads. To our knowledge, these findings represent the first comprehensive preclinical safety evaluation of VSV-EBOV vaccination during pregnancy and identify a critical window of vulnerability early in gestation. More broadly, this work underscores the central role of interferons in shaping placental immune responses and provides an experimental framework to guide evaluation of live-virus vaccines in pregnancy.

An integrated GIS and remote-sensing framework for district-level dengue risk assessment in northern India: development of a spatial Dengue Risk Index and assessment of its spatial concordance with reported incidence.
BACKGROUND: Dengue is an increasingly important vector-borne disease driven by climate variability, urbanization, environmental change, and population growth. Despite its rising burden in northern India, district-level spatial epidemiological frameworks integrating environmental suitability, transmission hazard, and population vulnerability remain limited. This study developed an integrated geographic information system (GIS)- and remote-sensing (RS)-based Dengue Risk Index (DRI) describing long-term spatial susceptibility to dengue in Gorakhpur district, Uttar Pradesh, and assessed its spatial concordance with reported dengue incidence. METHODS: A GIS-based multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) framework incorporating the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) integrated 14 environmental, topographic, hydrological, and socio-demographic variables into three thematic components: the Environmental Suitability Index (ESI; six variables), Hazard Index (HI; five variables), and Vulnerability Index (VI; three variables). Relative humidity and the Normalized Difference Moisture Index were excluded after redundancy screening. Rainfall was derived from India Meteorological Department (IMD) 0.25° daily gridded data for 2025, elevation from the Copernicus 30 m DEM, and population density from WorldPop 2025 constrained estimates. Standardized (1-5) raster layers were integrated using the Weighted Linear Combination (WLC) approach to construct the DRI. Spatial concordance between block-level mean DRI and laboratory-confirmed dengue incidence in 2025 (225 cases, 20 blocks) was assessed using Pearson's and Spearman's correlation, linear and negative binomial regression, influence diagnostics, and global Moran's I with Lagrange multiplier tests for spatial dependence. FINDINGS: The DRI (1-5 relative scale) showed marked spatial heterogeneity, with higher values in the central and western parts of the district. Chargawan, which contains Gorakhpur city, was the only block classified as Very High risk, followed by Sahjanwa, Piprauli, and Jungle Kaudia (High), whereas Brahmpur was classified as Very Low risk. Overall, 32.87% of the district (1,090.2 km2) was classified as High or Very High risk. The single very high-risk block accounted for 48.9% of reported cases. However, concordance between block-level DRI and incidence was weak and not statistically significant (Pearson's r = 0.16, p = 0.49; Spearman's ρ = -0.003, p = 0.99; R2 = 0.03; incidence rate ratio per 0.1 DRI = 1.05, 95% CI 0.91-1.21). Neither incidence nor the regression residuals showed significant spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I = -0.13 and -0.17; p ≥ 0.44), so spatial regression was not required. INTERPRETATION: The DRI provides a transparent, reproducible description of long-term spatial susceptibility to dengue that integrates environmental suitability, transmission hazard, and population vulnerability. Because its concordance with single-year, block-level incidence was weak and non-significant, it should not be interpreted as a predictor of dengue incidence or as a validated risk model. The framework may help district programs structure surveillance planning, but multi-year incidence, finer spatial units, and entomological data are needed before it is used to allocate interventions.

In silico multi-epitope vaccine design against Irkut virus using immunoinformatic and reverse vaccinology.
Irkut virus (IRKV) is a member of genus Lyssavirus, which leads to fatal encephalitis in humans and is primarily found in bats and dogs that transmit the virus to humans via bites/saliva. Most cases have been reported in Russia and in Siberia and recently in China. Whole genome sequencing has shown a number of codon changes in antigenic sites common to the Rabies vaccine reducing cross-protection, which makes IRKV a serious public health threat because of its high fatality. In this study, a multi-epitope vaccine against the IRKV glycoprotein was designed via reverse vaccinology approach. Seven B-cell, seven MHC-I, and seven MHC-II epitopes were selected. These epitopes have predicted HLA binding affinity and are non-allergen, and 12 out of 21 epitopes were fully conserved across the three circulating IRKV strains, whereas remaining nine carried out one or two substitutions. The chosen epitopes covered 99.57% of the world population. The final construct which included an adjuvant (EAAAK), epitopes, and a 6xHis tag was predicted to be highly antigenic (VaxiJen score 0.8112) and non-allergenic (AllerTop), showing no sequence mimicry with human proteins by BLASTp screening. The physicochemical analysis suggested that the construct was basic, hydrophilic, and stable (aliphatic index 68.11, instability index 37.5, pI 10.43, GRAVY -0.323). The 3D structure built using SWISS-MODEL and Phyre2 and refined by GalaxyRefine depicts that 95.1% of residues lie in the favored regions of the Ramachandran plot. The structural superposition with the native viral glycoprotein showed that the native fold was well preserved (core RMSD ≈ 2.4 Å). The molecular docking with TLR4 (minimum energy -1086.3) and normal mode analysis further suggested the stability of the receptor binding and structural integrity. C-ImmSim immune simulation with two doses (prime-boost) showed an enhanced secondary immune response following boost dose, manifested by a higher level of IgM, IgG, CD4+ T-helper cells activation, and cytokine production. The immune activation profile predicted was generally similar to that for the full-length G protein, and the CD8+ T-cell response was similar between the two antigens in the one simulation run. These results indicate that the multi-epitope construct vaccine is structurally stable and immunologically promising and can be used as a vaccine candidate for further experimental evaluation against Irkut virus.

Hepatitis E virus genome plasticity: a marker of chronicity and therapy failure?
Hepatitis E virus (HEV) is a globally distributed zoonotic pathogen, spread by contaminated food and blood products, and a leading cause of acute viral hepatitis. Recent data indicate that the HEV genome contains a highly heterogeneous hypervariable region (HVR) that can tolerate extensive genomic rearrangements, especially among immunocompromised patients. These rearrangements can increase HEV replication in tissue-culture and have further been observed in HEV-infected patients. Insertions comprise either duplications of virus-derived sequences, or alternatively, host-derived sequence fragments and exhibit enrichment of specific amino acids and functional motifs. However, the molecular mechanisms driving these insertions, as well as their functional significance, remain largely unexplored. Given that sequences not required for infectivity or replication are typically rapidly eliminated in small RNA viruses such as HEV, the persistence of HVR insertions suggests a potential biological role in HEV replication and/or pathogenesis. This review summarizes our current understanding of the role of HVR insertions during HEV infection, as well as the potential mechanisms underlying these insertions. We further discuss the factors driving the selection of genomic insertions and speculate on their functional role by analyzing over 650 publicly available HEV genotype 3 genome sequences and systematically cataloging identified insertions.

Neonatal mechanical ventilation.
Neonatal mechanical ventilation is a cornerstone in the management of respiratory failure in newborns (NBs), particularly in preterm infants, in whom pulmonary and neurologic increases their vulnerability to ventilation-induced lung injury. At present, the primary objective of respiratory support is to ensure adequate ventilation while minimizing lung and brain injury through lung-protective strategies and careful oxygen titration. Noninvasive ventilation (NIV) is currently the first-line approach for both initial respiratory support and post-extubation care, as it reduces the need for invasive ventilation and the incidence of ventilator-induced lung injury. Multiple modalities and devices are available, and their selection should be individualized according to the underlying disease, gestational age, and clinical response. The selection of the appropriate interface and ventilatory settings and patient-ventilator synchronization are of utmost importance. Noninvasive ventilation failure should be preceded by systematic optimization and requires well-defined criteria for timely therapeutic escalation. Conventional mechanical ventilation continues to be necessary in more severe cases. Its use should be synchronized and volume-targeted whenever possible, as this strategy has been shown to reduce major complications such as pneumothorax, intraventricular hemorrhage, and the composite outcome of death or bronchopulmonary dysplasia. High-frequency oscillatory ventilation serves as a rescue strategy in refractory cases and selected clinical condition, relying on the maintenance of lung recruitment with extremely low tidal volumes. Finally, ventilatory management of the most common neonatal respiratory conditions-such as respiratory distress syndrome, meconium aspiration syndrome, air leak syndrome, and bronchopulmonary dysplasia-requires a dynamic, individualized approach focused on lung protection from the earliest hours of life.

Occurrence and distribution of Sapovirus in shellfish.
Shellfish harbour emerging enteric viruses including sapovirus that are often not the main target for routine shellfish safety screening. Thus, the present investigation aimed at assessing the occurrence of sapovirus in 2450 shellfish samples using standard procedures and random-intercept logistic-regression modelling. The overall prevalence of shellfish-borne sapovirus was 17.14% (95% CI: 8.95-30.34). Sapovirus prevalence in shellfish was significantly different (p ≤ 0.0005) by shellfish type, family, genus, species, RNA extraction, nation and continent. Cockles (Cardiidae) showed the highest pooled sapovirus prevalence (∼26%), followed by clams (∼13%) and oysters (∼11). Among species, Perna spp had high-pooled sapovirus rate (66.5%), while Crassostrea gigas had 14%. Also, Sapovirus prevalence in shellfish was highest in Spain (35.8%), Brazil (25.3%), Italy (18.2%) and Japan (17.2%). By continent, South America (25.3%) and Europe (14.3%), pooled sapovirus rates in shellfish exceeded Asia (10.31%) and Africa (11.6%). The study identified detection methods and RNA extraction kits (as significant moderators) affect the ability to detect and accurately determine sapovirus prevalence (p≈0.05) in shellfish. Among 9 factors tested, nation and detection assays moderated sapovirus prevalence in shellfish significantly. Notably, shellfish species, genus, nation, kit, continent, family, detection assay, shellfish type, viral quality control, year, and sample size explained 67.27%, 56.93%, 55.48%, 43.51%, 38.92%, 35.89%, 28.14%, 23.36%, 18.06%, 4.74%, and 1.81%, respectively of the true variance in sapovirus pooled prevalence in shellfish. In conclusion, this study reveals that sapovirus contamination of shellfish is common. The pooled sapovirus prevalence in shellfish, with especially high rates in certain bivalves and locales, highlights sapovirus as a shellfish safety concern on par with norovirus. The findings underscore the importance of including sapovirus in routine shellfish monitoring and shellfish-linked outbreak investigations, complementing norovirus surveillance.

Beyond RSV: why the bronchiolitis burden in infants will not simply disappear.
Nirsevimab and maternal respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccination are delivering real-world important reductions in RSV-bronchiolitis hospitalisations, a landmark achievement in paediatric preventive medicine. We argue, however, that these successes should not be mistaken for the resolution of severe bronchiolitis as a clinical and public health problem. First, RSV's epidemiological dominance may partly reflect its transmission efficiency rather than a unique pathogenic superiority: rhinovirus, human metapneumovirus, adenovirus, and bocavirus already cause substantial disease, and genetic variants in CDHR3, GSDMB, and innate immune genes indicate that host susceptibility, not pathogen identity, is a key driver of severity. Second, although current evidence does not support viral replacement, the possibility that other respiratory viruses could expand into the ecological niche vacated by suppressed RSV transmission warrants close monitoring, alongside the theoretical, fitness-limited risk of nirsevimab-resistant RSV escape variants. Third, important gaps remain in long-term virological surveillance, cost-effectiveness evaluation, and equitable global access, particularly for the low- and middle-income countries that bear over 97% of RSV-attributable mortality. Conclusion: We contend that bronchiolitis should be understood as a syndrome reflecting the infant airway's stereotyped response to viral injury, rather than a disease defined by a single pathogen. Sustained broad-spectrum surveillance, transparent cost-effectiveness monitoring, and continued investment in a pan-respiratory mucosal vaccine pipeline are needed to ensure that early success against RSV translates into a durable reduction of the overall infant bronchiolitis burden. What is Known: • Nirsevimab and maternal RSV vaccination are producing substantial real-world reductions in RSV-bronchiolitis hospitalisations, a major success in paediatric preventive medicine. What is New: • We argue that the control of RSV does not equate to the control of severe infant bronchiolitis. Other respiratory viruses-rhinovirus, human metapneumovirus, adenovirus and bocavirus-already cause substantial disease and could expand into the ecological niche left by suppressed RSV transmission, while host genetic susceptibility, not pathogen identity, remains a key driver of severity. We call for sustained broad spectrum viral surveillance to ensure that success against RSV translates into a durable reduction of the overall bronchiolitis burden, rather than its replacement by other pathogens.

Multi-species plasmids and K. pneumoniae clonal spread contribute to bla NDM outbreak across seven UK healthcare sites.
OBJECTIVES: The NDM carbapenemase enables Gram-negative bacteria to hydrolyse almost all β-lactam antibiotics. In 2023, a large increase of bla NDM in clinical isolates was identified in a clinical microbiology laboratory serving hospitals and GP practices in Merseyside, UK, raising concerns of a larger outbreak. METHODS: We used short-read WGS and bioinformatic analyses to identify the outbreak(s) and identify potential links by combining with anonymized, routinely collected clinical metadata. A subset of isolates were long-read sequenced to analyse resistance genes and plasmids at maximum resolution. RESULTS: The outbreak included Enterobacter hormaechei, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Escherichia coli, Citrobacter freundii, Citrobacter braakii and Enterobacter kobei and 28 STs. K. pneumoniae ST101 represented the only major clonal expansion (18/21 K. pneumoniae isolates), and combination with metadata strongly suggested a multi-site hospital-associated outbreak. We identified four variants of bla NDM, and long-read sequencing indicated bla NDM-1 spread across species was driven by an IncHI2/IncHI2A plasmid, representing 82% of bla NDM1 isolates. CONCLUSIONS: This study captured an outbreak of bla NDM-positive Enterobacterales across eight healthcare settings and highlights the complex epidemiology of spread mediated by both expansion of successful lineages (K. pneumoniae ST101) and multi-species plasmids (IncHI2/IncHI2A). It also highlights the challenge of recognizing and tracing an outbreak linked to patients moving across different healthcare systems and the importance of linked surveillance systems.

WHO Bacterial Priority Pathogens List: a 32-year global trend and inequality analysis of antimicrobial resistance burden by age and region.
INTRODUCTION: The WHO Bacterial Priority Pathogens List identifies antibiotic-resistant bacteria posing a serious health threat. We aimed to analyse age-specific and region-specific burden trajectories and inequalities across countries with different socio-development levels for these pathogens. METHODS: We conducted a systematic analysis (1990-2021) using the Global Burden of Disease Study's Measuring Infectious Causes and Resistance Outcomes for Burden Estimation database, assessing trends and inequalities in mortality burden attributable to priority pathogens by age and region. Analyses included age-period-cohort modelling, average annual percentage change (AAPC) and health inequality metrics across countries stratified by sociodemographic index (SDI). RESULTS: Global mortality attributable to priority antibiotic-resistant pathogens rose from 5.47 to 6.12 per 100 000 in 1990-2021 (annual net drift: 0.086%). By age, mortality declined in under 5 but increased in the middle-aged and elderly (peaking at 40-44 and ≥95), primarily driven by carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella (AAPC 2.1%-2.4%) and Escherichia coli (AAPC 1.6%-2.2%). Mortality from multidrug-resistant tuberculosis rose across all ages, particularly in neonates (AAPC 7.4%, 95% CI 6.6% to 8.1%). Regionally, high-income Asia Pacific saw the steepest mortality decline (AAPC -2.5%, 95% CI -2.7% to -2.3%), while Eastern Europe exhibited the sharpest increase (AAPC 1.2%, 95% CI 0.2% to 2.2%), fueled by multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (AAPC 7.7%, 95% CI 6.0% to 9.5%), carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella (AAPC 3.5%, 95% CI 2.2% to 4.9%) and vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus (AAPC 3.1%, 95% CI 1.5% to 4.7%). Southern sub-Saharan Africa experienced a rise in fluoroquinolone-resistant Salmonella Typhi (AAPC 4.6%, 95% CI 2.5% to 6.8%). Over the 32-year period, the slope index of inequality in mortality burden of priority pathogens narrowed from -333.65 to -282.20, while the concentration index widened from -0.28 to -0.31. CONCLUSIONS: The global mortality burden of priority antibiotic-resistant pathogens increased between 1990 and 2021, with age and regional disparities demanding targeted containment. Higher burden in low-SDI regions requires equitable healthcare resource allocation to combat antimicrobial resistance.

Two-component system VraSR senses host defense peptide PMAP-36 to promote Streptococcus suis pathogenicity through regulating accD expression.
Streptococcus suis (S. suis) is an important zoonotic pathogen that causes severe infections in humans and animals worldwide. Upon infection, the host innate immune system produces host defense peptides (HDPs) to resist S. suis invasion. PMAP-36, a porcine-derived HDP, has been shown to fail to kill S. suis, suggesting that this pathogen has evolved strategies to evade PMAP-36-mediated immune defense. However, the exact mechanism by which S. suis responds to PMAP-36 remains unclear. Here we showed that PMAP-36 significantly enhanced S. suis adhesion, cytotoxicity, and virulence gene expression. The two-component system (TCS) VraSR was essential for PMAP-36 to promote S. suis pathogenicity. We demonstrated that PMAP-36 directly bound to the sensor kinase VraS. Further transcriptomic analysis revealed that VraSR sensed PMAP-36 to regulate fatty acid biosynthesis, in which a key gene accD expression was significantly downregulated in both PMAP-36-treated ΔvraS and ΔvraR mutant strains. Deletion of accD attenuates S. suis in vivo pathogenicity, including reduced bacterial loads, alleviated organ damage, and decreased inflammatory response. Additionally, VraSR-mediated accD expression was critical for S. suis-induced cytotoxicity and inflammatory response, as deletion of vraS or vraR fails to reduce inflammatory cytokines production due to sustained high accD expression. This study reveals VraSR-mediated virulence regulatory mechanism in response to HDP activation, which provides new insight into the development of novel strategies to combat S. suis infection.

Design, synthesis, antibacterial activity, and mechanistic studies of Ebselen derivatives against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
The rapid emergence of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) necessitates the development of novel antibacterial agents with distinct mechanisms of action. Ebselen, has shown promising antibacterial activity through disruption of redox homeostasis. However, its poor aqueous solubility and limited therapeutic potential call for further structural optimization. In this study, 29 ebselen derivatives were designed and synthesized to systematically explore structure-activity relationships (SAR) and improve antibacterial efficacy. Antibacterial profiling evaluation identified the most potent compound HX-27, which exhibited strong activity against MRSA, with minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) as low as 2 μM. Its MBC was >16 μM, indicating predominantly bacteriostatic activity at low concentrations. Moreover, HX-27 demonstrated rapid bactericidal activity and effectively inhibited biofilm formation with low hemolytic activity and minimal cytotoxicity. Mechanistic investigations revealed that HX-27 exerts a pronounced membrane-disruptive effect, leading to loss of membrane integrity and bacterial cell death. Integrated metabolomic and proteomic analyses further demonstrated that ebselen derivatives induce significant perturbations in sulfur-containing amino acid metabolism and intracellular redox balance, while also affecting central metabolic pathways and protein transport systems. These results indicate that the antibacterial activity of ebselen derivatives arises from multi-target mechanisms involving both membrane disruption and metabolic dysregulation. Notably, HX-27 displayed satisfactory aqueous solubility and excellent in vivo efficacy in a Galleria mellonella infection model, significantly improving survival under severe infection conditions. Overall, this study establishes a comprehensive structure-activity-mechanism framework for ebselen derivatives and identifies promising lead compounds for the development of novel therapeutics against drug-resistant bacterial infections.

Drug-resistant tuberculosis in children: from global estimates to urgent action.
New estimates suggest a substantial burden of drug-resistant tuberculosis in children and young adolescents. This editorial proposes an action plan to address gaps in prevention, case detection and treatment of drug-resistant TB in these age groups. https://bit.ly/4bxoP0M

Bovine leptospirosis: Pathogenic species and serovars of Leptospira associated with dairy cows.
Leptospirosis is an economically important zoonotic bacterial infection of livestock that causes abortions, stillbirths, infertility, and loss of milk production. Bovine leptospirosis occurs worldwide and is caused by infection with pathogenic bacteria in the genus Leptospira that can colonize the kidney or genital tract of both males and females to maintain disease transmission via shedding in urine, the reproductive tract, or via vertical transmission to a fetus. Cattle are a reservoir host for L. borgpetersenii serovar Hardjo but can also shed other pathogenic species and serovars associated with bovine infection and zoonotic transmission. In this observational study, urine samples (n = 384) were collected from dairy cows in a California slaughterhouse to test for the presence of pathogenic Leptospira. In total, 56 urine samples (15%) were positive, with 55 (14%) positive by lipL32 rtPCR and 24 (6%) positive by culture. Characterization of cultured isolates identified L. borgpetersenii serovar Hardjo (n = 18), L. interrogans serovar Pomona (n = 5), and L. interrogans serovar Copenhageni (n = 1). Leptospira targeted amplicon sequencing analysis of 32 lipL32 PCR-positive but culture-negative urine samples identified 23 as positive for L. borgpetersenii, one as positive for a mixed infection comprising L. borgpetersenii and L. santarosai, and 4 as positive for L. santarosai; 4 remained undefined. Phylogenetics identified a new genotype of L. borgpetersenii that was not readily amenable to culture using current medium formulations. The identification of species and serovars of Leptospira currently circulating in cattle is critical for efficacious surveillance, diagnostic, and prevention strategies.

One-pot dual RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a lateral flow biosensor for rapid detection of carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae.
Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) poses a major public health threat due to high mortality and limited therapeutic options. Rapid and accurate detection of both species identity and resistance determinants is critical for clinical management. Here, we developed a dual-target recombinase polymerase amplification-CRISPR/Cas12a multiplex lateral flow assay (DRC-MLFA) for simultaneous detection of K. pneumoniae and blaKPC in a single reaction. This platform introduces a functionally differentiated dual-channel detection strategy, in which the K. pneumoniae signal is generated directly via RPA-lateral flow readout, while blaKPC detection is achieved through an additional CRISPR/Cas12a-mediated verification step. To enable one-pot integration, suboptimal protospacer adjacent motif (PAM) sequences were employed to delay Cas12a activation, thereby coordinating amplification and CRISPR detection within a single reaction system. Under optimized conditions, the assay achieved dual-target detection within 50 min at 37 °C, with a limit of detection of 101 CFU/μL and high specificity against non-target pathogens. Validation with 30 clinical samples showed strong concordance with quantitative PCR. This portable and low-cost biosensor provides a practical solution for point-of-care detection of CRKP and establishes a framework for integrating hierarchical specificity control into multiplex CRISPR diagnostics.

Antivirulence Benzothiophenes Inhibit Intracellular Mycobacterium tuberculosis by Targeting the Sensor Histidine Kinase MprB.
Pulmonary tuberculosis remains one of the most prevalent and threatening infectious diseases. Classical anti-tubercular therapy targets essential enzymes of the pathogen Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), thereby suppressing bacterial growth. However, the emergence of drug-resistant strains necessitates alternative therapeutic approaches. Virulence inhibition is a promising strategy that blocks Mtb virulence factors required for survival within host cells. We previously identified a hit compound, BTP15, which protected fibroblasts and THP-1 macrophages from Mtb-induced cell death ex vivo by blocking phagosomal escape through inhibition of the mycobacterial histidine kinase MprB. Due to poor pharmacokinetics, the structure of BTP15 was optimized. New benzothiophene derivatives were screened for MprB inhibition, microsomal stability, toxicity, and ex vivo efficacy in THP-1 and MRC-5 cells. The lead compound, 7a, exhibited favorable pharmacokinetic parameters, showed no toxicity in mice at 250 mg/kg, and prevented Mtb dissemination in an acute mouse model of tuberculosis.

Synthesis and biological assessment of silver nanoparticles using Adiantum incisum extracts.
Silver nanoparticles (Ag NPs) were synthesized using methanolic and ethanolic extracts of Adiantum incisum and evaluated different biological activities. The synthesis of Ag NPs was confirmed by color change and UV-vis spectroscopy absorption peak at 400-500 nm. Furthermore, optimized biosynthesis by adjusting parameters such as temperature (50-65 °C for methanolic extract and 35 °C for ethanolic extract), pH (Optimum pH 9-10), and various salt concentrations (0.2 mL NaCl showed maximum stability). Additionally, the characterization of silver nanoparticles was performed using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) which revealed the presence of functional groups involved in capping and reduction, X-ray diffraction (XRD) which confirmed the face-centered cubic crystalline structure, energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) confirmed the presence of elemental silver, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) revealed monodispersed spherical particles. Similarly, the biological activities of plant extracts and synthesized silver nanoparticles were evaluated. Insecticidal assays against Tribolium castaneum showed 56.7% and 53.4% mortality for methanolic and ethanolic Ag NPs at 1000 µg/mL. Phytotoxicity tests against Lemna minor indicated 51.11% inhibition for ethanolic-extract synthesized Ag NPs, while 45.5% inhibition for methanolic-extract synthesized Ag NPs. Antioxidant activity assessed using the 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) assay revealed 85.2% inhibition for ethanolic Ag NPs and 64.96% inhibition for methanolic Ag NPs at 500 µg/mL. The analgesic potential was evaluated using the acetic acid-induced writhing test, where ethanolic silver nanoparticles demonstrated 65.2% inhibition and methanolic silver nanoparticles 61.11% inhibition at 500 µg/mL. The anti-inflammatory activity showed 79.2% inhibition for methanolic Ag NPs and 75% inhibition for ethanolic Ag NPs at 300 µg/mL. Antibacterial assays against Shigella dysenteriae and Pseudomonas aureginosa showed inhibition zone of 22 mm against S. dysenteriae and 20 mm against P. aureginosa for ethanolic Ag NPs and 22 mm against S. dysenteriae and 18 mm against P. aureginosa for methanolic Ag NPs. Antifungal activity against Aspergillus niger also showed a notable inhibition zone, where methanolic silver nanoparticles showed 14 mm and ethanolic silver nanoparticles showed 12 mm inhibition at 100 µg/mL. Furthermore, some parameters such as particle size or surface charge are the shortcomings of the study. These findings demonstrate that the biosynthesis of silver nanoparticles from A. incisum extracts exhibits significant biological activities, highlighting their potential applications in pharmaceutical and agricultural fields.

BCG at 100: The Paradox of an Indispensable Vaccine.
Bacille Calmette-Guerin (BCG) vaccine, in use for over a century, occupies a paradoxical position in global health. It protects infants against disseminated tuberculosis (TB) with 60-80% efficacy and reduces all-cause infant mortality through non-specific effects mediated by trained immunity. Yet it provides limited and variable protection against pulmonary TB in adolescents and adults who drive transmission. A tuberculin survey from western Uttar Pradesh documented an annual risk of TB infection of 3.5-4.1%, nearly 50 times the national target, in a predominantly BCG-vaccinated child population. This perspective addresses four fundamental questions: Has BCG become redundant for its original purpose? Can it be improved? Is it more efficacious for non-TB indications? And is it currently indispensable? The pipeline is reviewed from a pediatric prism, identifying preferred candidates for each age group. MTBVAC leads as the most promising infant BCG replacement candidate while M72/AS01E is a frontrunner for adolescents and adults.

Draft genome sequences and antimicrobial susceptibility profiles of one K1 and five K2 clinical hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from Ghana.
We report the draft genome sequences of six clinical hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from Ghana. These isolates carry critical hypervirulence determinants, including siderophores and hypermucoidy regulators. These genomic sequences significantly enrich the West African data set on hypervirulent K. pneumoniae, providing vital baselines to support the surveillance of emerging high-risk lineages.

Antifungal resistance landscapes in major fungal pathogens in Zhejiang, China.
BACKGROUND: Invasive fungal infections caused by Aspergillus fumigatus and other pathogenic fungi represent a major global health threat, with treatment increasingly complicated by the emergence of antifungal drug resistance. Azole antifungals serve as the first-line therapy for aspergillosis, but resistance rates vary substantially across geographical regions. This study aimed to characterize the antifungal resistance landscape among clinical fungal isolates from Hangzhou and Yiwu cities in Zhejiang Province, Eastern China, and to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying azole resistance in Aspergillus fumigatus. RESULTS: We analyzed 110 Aspergillus clinical isolates for antifungal susceptibility. Among A. fumigatus strains, 8.6% exhibited azole resistance, with half of these harboring the tandem repeat mutation TR34/L98H in the cyp51A gene. One resistant strain carried the TR46/Y121F/T289A mutation combination. Minimum inhibitory concentration testing revealed that 8.6% of A. fumigatus isolates were resistant to amphotericin B We identified one resistant isolate without known resistance mutations and characterized it through whole-genome sequencing and transcriptomic analysis. Novel mutations S437F in cyp51A and P298T in hmg1 were discovered; however, functional validation using CRISPR-Cas9 demonstrated these mutations do not directly confer resistance. Instead, transcriptomic profiling revealed significant upregulation of ergosterol biosynthesis pathway genes and efflux transporter genes, suggesting alternative resistance mechanisms. Among non-A. fumigatus species, all A. niger isolates displayed resistance to itraconazole and posaconazole. CONCLUSIONS: This comprehensive regional surveillance reveals concerning patterns of antifungal resistance among major human pathogenic fungi in Zhejiang Province, China. The identification of both classical resistance mutations and novel transcription-mediated resistance mechanisms highlights the complex and evolving nature of antifungal resistance. These findings emphasize the critical need for continued surveillance programs and rapid resistance detection methods to inform clinical treatment strategies and improve patient outcomes.

Bronchoscopic phenotypes and anatomical airway involvement in invasive tracheobronchial aspergillosis without classic immunosuppression: association with in-hospital mortality.
BACKGROUND: The prognostic relevance of visual bronchoscopic phenotyping and airway lesion extent in invasive tracheobronchial aspergillosis (ITBA) without classic immunosuppression remains unclear. This study aimed to describe the clinical, radiological and bronchoscopic features of ITBA, and to evaluate the association between visual bronchoscopic assessment and in-hospital mortality. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study at National Lung Hospital in Hanoi, Vietnam, from January 2023 to December 2025. Adult patients with histopathologically proven ITBA lacking classic immunosuppressive factors were included. On bronchoscopy, patients were dichotomised by the predominance of pseudomembranes and an airway involvement score was calculated to assess the extent of the lesions. RESULTS: The study included 31 patients with proven ITBA (mean age 61.4 years; 83.9% male). Diabetes (41.9%), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (29.0%) were the most common comorbidities, and 16.1% of the cohort were immunocompetent. Bronchoscopy revealed the pseudomembranous phenotype in 61.3% of patients. Overall in-hospital mortality was 29.0%. While the pseudomembranous phenotype was more frequent among deceased patients than survivors (88.9% vs. 50.0%), this difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.101). In contrast, deceased patients had a significantly higher median airway involvement score (3 points vs. 2 points; p = 0.007), indicating more extensive disease. No major procedural complications occurred. CONCLUSION: ITBA can manifest in patients without classic immunosuppression. Beyond the diagnostic utility, bronchoscopy may provide prognostic relevance for this selected cohort, particularly through evaluation of the anatomical extent of airway involvement, rather than visual bronchoscopic phenotyping.

High Prevalence of Stunting, Wasting, and Underweight in Children Younger Than 5 Years Old in Mopeia District, Rural Mozambique.
Mozambique has stunting, wasting, and underweight rates of 37%, 15%, and 4%, respectively. In Zambézia Province, Mozambique, 44.6% of children younger than 5 years of age suffer from chronic malnutrition, which impairs physical and cognitive development and leads to long-term health and productivity issues. This study examines undernutrition, stunting, wasting, underweight, and their associations with socioeconomic status among children younger than 5 years old in Mopeia District, Zambézia Province (central Mozambique). We conducted a secondary analysis of data from the Broad One Health Endectocide-Based Malaria Intervention in Africa 2021 cluster randomized clinical trial, which included a cohort of 2,667 children younger than 5 years old. We calculated odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals to assess associations between risk factors and undernutrition. The prevalence rates of stunting, wasting, and underweight were 41.7%, 20.4%, and 24.3%, respectively; these numbers are among the highest globally. Lower wealth index showed an association with higher odds of stunting and underweight, whereas distance from tarmac roads showed a link to increased wasting. Key predictors of stunting included lack of electricity, long water-fetching times, and smaller household size; being underweight showed an association with the number of bed nets and housing type. These relationships reflect socioeconomic patterns rather than direct causality. Undernutrition among children younger than 5 years old in Mopeia District remains critically high and is strongly patterned by socioeconomic factors. Addressing structural determinants, such as household wealth, access to infrastructure, and living conditions, will be essential for reducing the burden of undernutrition in rural Mozambique.

Cost-effectiveness of end-game strategies against sleeping sickness across the Democratic Republic of Congo.
BACKGROUND: Gambiense human African trypanosomiasis (gHAT) is marked for elimination of transmission (EoT) by 2030. We examined the cost-effectiveness (CE) of EoT in the Democratic Republic of Congo, the country with the highest burden. METHODS: In 165 health zones (HZs), we modelled the transmission dynamics, health outcomes, and economic costs of six strategies during 2026-40, including cessation activities once reported cases reach zero. Uncertainty in CE was assessed within the net monetary framework, presenting optimal strategies across willingness-to-pay (WTP) values, in costs per disability-adjusted life-year averted. We assessed the optimal strategy for CE and EoT in each health zone separately, but present results by health zone, by coordination, and for the whole country. RESULTS: Status quo strategies, CE strategies (WTP = $500), and strategies with a high probability of EoT by 2030 are predicted to yield EoT by 2030 in 118 HZs, 123 HZs, and 134 HZs respectively, at a cost by 2040 of $67.8M [95% PI: $36.7M-113M], $93.3M [95% PI: $51.6M-153M], $185M [95% PI: $111M-309M]. A more lenient timeline of EoT by 2040 would lead to EoT in 152 HZs at a cost of $158M [95% PI: $91.6-265M], leaving 13 HZs shy of the goal. Costs would have to be front-loaded; in 2026, while status quo strategies would cost $8.75M [95% PI: $7.01M-11.2M], elimination strategies would cost $27.0 [95% PI: $21.0M-35.2M]. Investing in EoT by 2030 is predicted to reduce 68% of gHAT deaths from 7979 [95% PI: 770-27,868] with status quo strategies to 2576 [95% PI: 255-9133]. CONCLUSIONS: Current tools could make considerable progress to maximise the probability of EoT by 2030, but novel tools could help in select health zones are facing a low probability of EoT even with more ambitious strategies.

Adaptive metabolic reprogramming of the brain tissue during late-stage Trypanosoma brucei infection maintains host learning and memory.
Human African Trypanosomiasis (HAT) is a two-stage infection caused by Trypanosoma brucei ssp. In stage I the trypanosomes are in blood, lymph and tissue interstitial space and the infection progresses to stage II when the parasites enter the central nervous system (CNS), resulting in behavioural aberrations that proceed to coma and death. Here, we use a bioluminescent murine model of HAT to examine parasite localisation and the changes in host brain gene expression, metabolism and function, and behaviour that occur over the course of the infection. The murine HAT model reproduces the decrease in brain tryptophan well established in clinical samples, and we report for the first time an unprecedented 1.8-fold decrease in global brain glucose metabolism in stage II infection. These metabolic changes are accompanied by an 18-fold decrease in brain insulin transcripts without changes in pathways regulating the cellular responses to insulin. By contrast, genes involved in fatty acid and lipid metabolism are upregulated in the brain during stage II infection. Moreover, we show that transcriptional programmes regulating mitochondrial metabolism dynamically adapts across the time course of HAT infection, ultimately leading to a transcriptional programme that diverts host brain metabolism away from glycolysis during stage II infection. Overall, our data demonstrate a reprogramming of brain energy metabolism during stage II HAT infection that favours the utilization of fatty acids and lipids to meet the energy demands of the brain, with a reduced reliance on glucose metabolism. Despite the profound neurometabolic changes observed, host anxiety-like behaviour is unchanged and episodic learning and memory is not impaired, suggesting that brain metabolic reprogramming enables the utilisation of adipose reserves to maintain core brain functions. These finding may explain the progressive onset of neurological symptoms in HAT patients and inform the development therapeutic interventions to alleviate them.

Water, sanitation, and hygiene in soil-transmitted helminth control: A scoping review of evidence gaps across transmission pathways.
Soil-transmitted helminths (STH) are parasitic intestinal worms infecting humans through contact with, or ingestion of, soil contaminated with eggs shed by infected individuals. STHs include roundworms (Ascaris lumbricoides, Strongyloides stercoralis), whipworm (Trichuris trichiura) and hookworms (Ancylostoma duodenale, Necator americanus, Ancylostoma ceylanicum). Their transmission is influenced by water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services and practices. Unlike past reviews, this scoping review did not assess effect sizes or strength of associations. Instead, it aimed to: map WASH-related risk factors in relation to STH infection; assess whether these align with plausible transmission pathways and conceptual frameworks; and characterise methodological features of the evidence base, including diagnostic approaches, that affect comparability of findings. We analysed 197 studies, of which 174 were observational and 23 were intervention studies. We found a substantial and growing body of evidence examining the relationship between WASH and other environmental exposures and the prevalence and intensity of STH infection. Nonetheless, important aspects such as food chain pathways, environmental surveillance, under-studied species, and measures of service and infrastructure uptake and use, quality, and community coverage over time, remain under-investigated, hampering drawing practical conclusions for improvement of service delivery. Existing and new research can be enhanced in several areas. Routine investigations like prevalence surveys should apply standard WASH definitions to reduce heterogeneity, and apply a conceptual framework of transmission in study design. Intervention studies should be based on theories of change that map actions disrupting transmission pathways, implementing a comprehensive intervention package and examining factors affecting behaviours or intervention compliance. Evaluation of intervention uptake should also be included. New research should address the evidence gaps identified, and incorporate timelines with realistic likelihood of impact into study planning and proposals, given the environmental persistence of certain STH species and the fact that developing lasting and sustained behaviour change can be slow.

Interventions to address the effects of climate change on human health in sub-Saharan Africa: A scoping review.
Climate change poses disproportionate threats to human health in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), yet comprehensive evidence on implemented interventions remains under-researched. Understanding the scope and characteristics of existing climate-health interventions is essential for informing policy priorities and action in the region. We conducted a scoping review following Arksey and O'Malley's framework and PRISMA-ScR reporting guidelines. We systematically searched Google Scholar, PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus for peer-reviewed empirical studies on climate-health interventions in SSA, with no date restrictions. Two reviewers independently screened 3009 records. A total of 36 studies reporting 350 interventions were included. The majority of the studies (83.3%) focused exclusively on adaptation, while a smaller proportion (16.7%) combined both adaptation and mitigation strategies. Four overarching intervention categories were identified inductively from the included studies, each comprising distinct but conceptually related sub-categories: health systems strengthening and governance; disease surveillance, monitoring, and early warning; environmental health and infrastructure; and community resilience and social wellbeing. Vector-borne diseases, particularly malaria, constituted the primary health focus, while heat-related illnesses, occupational health, and mental health received limited attention. Studies mostly reported interventions in West Africa, East Africa, Southern Africa, and multi-regional settings, with Central Africa receiving limited attention. The evidence is predominantly rural-focused (n = 18; 50%), with urban-focused studies accounting for 10 studies (27.8%) and mixed urban-rural settings for the remaining 8 (22.2%). Notably, no dedicated study investigated interventions specifically targeting coastal areas. People-centred interventions predominated over nature-based solutions. Key evidence gaps included cross-sectional study designs limiting causal inference, insufficient cost-effectiveness evaluations, limited integration of indigenous knowledge, and inadequate attention to gender-specific and occupational vulnerabilities. Policy efforts must go beyond disease-specific responses toward integrated strategies addressing multiple climate-health pathways while prioritising underrepresented regions and mitigation opportunities to build comprehensive, equitable climate resilience across the region.

Cyclosporiasis in Solid Organ and Hematopoietic Cell Transplant Recipients: Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention.
BACKGROUND: Cyclospora cayetanensis is a foodborne coccidian protozoan that causes prolonged, often relapsing watery diarrhea. Once considered largely a travel-associated infection, it has become a recurring cause of large, domestically acquired, produce-associated outbreaks in temperate countries. The 2026 US season was the largest on record and prompted a CDC Health Advisory, placing substantial numbers of solid organ transplant (SOT) and hematopoietic cell transplant (HCT) recipients at risk of exposure. AIM: To provide a practical, transplant-specific approach to the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of cyclosporiasis, using the 2026 outbreak as a worked example of a problem that will recur in future seasons. OBSERVATIONS: As of August 17 2026, CDC had reported 15 716 laboratory-confirmed domestically acquired cases since May 1, including 828 hospitalizations and two deaths, with at least 11 841 further cases under investigation; 1180 cases were reported during the whole of the 2025 season. A large multistate outbreak was traced to shredded iceberg lettuce sourced from central Mexico. Published data describing cyclosporiasis in transplant recipients are limited to small case series and seven individual case reports that provide detailed clinical descriptions. Among these seven reported cases, all occurred in SOT recipients more than one year after transplantation, none were receiving trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) prophylaxis at the time of diagnosis, and chronic watery diarrhea with weight loss predominated. Stool polymerase chain reaction (PCR), usually within a multiplex gastrointestinal panel, is the preferred diagnostic test, as routine ova-and-parasite examination does not reliably detect the parasite; unstained oocysts are easily mistaken for yeast or debris unless modified acid-fast or safranin staining or ultraviolet autofluorescence is specifically applied. TMP-SMX remains the treatment of choice; longer treatment courses may be required in immunocompromised patients, and secondary prophylaxis may be considered in select patients. Because person-to-person transmission is unlikely, Contact Precautions are only recommended for diapered or incontinent patients, and environmental control depends on mechanical removal because the bilayered oocyst wall resists chemical disinfection. CONCLUSION: Cyclospora should be considered in any transplant recipient with persistent or relapsing diarrhea during the May-August season, irrespective of travel history. Clinicians should specifically request Cyclospora testing, obtain stool PCR early, treat with TMP-SMX, and reinforce food- and water-safety counseling. The 2026 outbreak demonstrates how rapidly population exposure can escalate, and the same approach will apply to future seasons. Published transplant-specific experience remains strikingly limited.

A smartphone-integrated plasmonic biosensor for amplification-free detection of African swine fever virus.
African Swine Fever Virus (ASFV) poses a catastrophic threat to global swine production, with recent outbreaks across Europe, Asia, and the Caribbean, significantly elevating the biosecurity risk to the United States' billion-dollar pork industry. Current diagnostic gold standards are laboratory-dependent and introduce critical delays in outbreak response. To address this gap, a plasmonic biosensor based on functionalized gold nanoparticles (GNPs) was developed for the rapid, amplification-free detection of ASFV. GNPs were surface-functionalized with 11-mercaptoundecanoic acid (MUDA) and combined in situ with ASFV-specific oligonucleotide probes targeting a conserved region of the p72 (B646L) gene. The detection mechanism relies on acid-induced aggregation: hybridization of target ASFV DNA to the probe generates a rigid duplex that shields the nanoparticles from acid-induced destabilization, maintaining a ruby-red color, whereas in the absence of target DNA the GNPs aggregate, producing a visible red-to-blue color shift. The optimized plasmonic biosensor demonstrated 100% analytical specificity, with no cross-reactivity against a panel of 19 non-target bacterial genomic DNA samples representative of the swine environment. Detection limits determined by the IUPAC 3σ criterion were 285 copies per reaction for Probe 1 and 402 copies per reaction for Probe 2, within the same order of magnitude as the qPCR reference assay run on the same dilution series (approximately 312 copies per reaction) under the experimental conditions used here. A smartphone-based Bio-Analytics App employing an RGB color-conversion algorithm served as a quantitative reader, yielding signal-to-noise ratios (S/N) that strongly correlated with benchtop spectrophotometric readings (A520/A620 ratio, R2 = 0.96) and achieved diagnostic concordance with qPCR binary calls. This platform offers a robust and low-cost (∼$2 per test), amplification-free approach to ASFV screening with potential for point-of-need deployment, subject to future validation in clinical specimens.

[Awake prone positioning in acute hypoxemic respiratory failure].
Prone Positioning (PP) improves oxygenation and reduces mortality in intubated patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome. Meanwhile, non-invasive oxygenation strategies have reduced the need for intubation in patients with Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure (AHRF). During the Covid-19 pandemic, the limited availability of invasive mechanical ventilation prompted interest in research on awake PP for non-intubated patients. Encouraging results in this population have led to ongoing studies investigating the benefit of PP for other causes. This simple and low-cost therapy could improve the management of non-intubated patients with AHRF. However, maintaining PP for a sufficient duration to achieve clinical benefit remains a major challenge.

COVID-19 in migrating people at the US-Mexico border during Title 42 immigration restrictions.
INTRODUCTION: In March 2020, the US government implemented the policy of 'Title 42,' which restricted entry of asylum seekers on the stated basis of COVID-19 prevention. In the subsequent years, informal settlements for displaced persons developed and increased in size near the US-Mexico border. We sought to determine the risk of COVID-19 in this setting and compare this to nearby communities at the border. METHODS: We conducted an observational study of COVID-19 using data from a humanitarian relief operation at informal settlements at the US-Mexico border from March 2020 to March 2021. People who used this clinic had travelled through irregular routes of migration in Latin America. We reviewed patient characteristics, symptoms and point-of-care SARS-CoV-2 test results during the study period. We compared COVID-19 percent positivity in the camp with the surrounding communities in Mexico and Texas, USA, over 4-week periods. RESULTS: In 6764 clinical encounters, there were 3737 SARS-CoV-2 tests completed with 482 positive results (12.9%, 95% CI 11.8% to 14.1%). Percent positivity was higher in people aged 30-39 years (16.5%) and 40-49 years (16.2%) compared with other age groups (p<0.001) and was 61.5% in pregnant women. Percent positivity was higher in asymptomatic people with suspected close contact exposures than in people with symptoms (15.2% vs 6.9%, p<0.001). Percent positivity was never higher in the camp than in the surrounding community in Matamoros, Tamaulipas, Mexico, and for 8 of the 13 4-week periods, not higher than in Cameron County, Texas. CONCLUSION: COVID-19 percent positivity was typically lower or the same in this population of migrating people as in the surrounding communities, which provides further evidence against the use of pandemic-era immigration restrictions through Title 42.

Lassa fever prediction using data from Nigeria's national surveillance registry.
Lassa fever is a dangerous viral illness that is endemic in Nigeria and clinically difficult to separate from malaria and other febrile conditions in its early phase, which delays diagnosis and treatment. Machine learning has been proposed as a triage aid, yet several reported successes rest on small samples. Using the openly available national surveillance dataset of 20,027 suspected cases, of which 15.8% were laboratory-confirmed, we predicted laboratory confirmation from pre-laboratory bedside features alone. Synthetic oversampling was confined to training folds. Nine classifiers, including soft-voting and stacking ensembles, were compared by stratified five-fold cross-validation and a held-out test set using metrics suited to imbalanced data, alongside calibration, SHAP, missing-data and decision-threshold analyses. Discrimination from bedside features was modest, with the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve reaching 0.719 in cross-validation and 0.709 on the test set. Logistic regression, selected by cross-validation, achieved the best balanced accuracy (0.652) and F1 score (0.377), and the higher test value of the soft-voting ensemble was not statistically distinguishable from it. Gradient-boosted ensembles reached the highest accuracy (about 0.85) but recall below 0.22. The strongest predictors of the logistic regression were ordinary symptoms and documented source-case contact, and its performance was unchanged in fully documented records (0.702). Symptom-based prediction offers a bounded triage aid rather than a substitute for laboratory confirmation, and the study provides a reproducible benchmark for machine learning in neglected tropical disease diagnosis. The code is available at https://github.com/EgwuSamuel/lassa-fever-benchmark.

Arthropod-Related Health Threats (ARHTs) and Nuisance Arthropods in North Khorasan Province, Iran: A Comprehensive Review.
The arthropod vectors, such as mosquitoes, sand flies, and ticks, transmit various pathogens to humans and animals, leading to public health issues. Therefore, an effective disease surveillance system is essential to provide information on these diseases in order to monitor their trends worldwide. The current study focused on the prevalence of arthropod-borne diseases and their vectors in North Khorasan Province located in northeastern Iran, bordering Turkmenistan. A narrative literature review was conducted to analyze the status of arthropod-related health threats (ARHTs) and their vectors in this area. Sources with no time limit up to 2025 were examined from PubMed, Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science databases using keywords like vector, arthropod, North Khorasan, and Iran. After excluding duplicates and irrelevant content, a final list of 31 papers was thoroughly evaluated. This province exhibits the occurrence of several major ARHTs, including visceral leishmaniasis, cutaneous leishmaniasis, West Nile fever, chikungunya, Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever, Q fever, Theileria infection, equine piroplasmosis, dirofilariasis, Dipylidium caninum infection, fascioliasis, hymenolepiasis, scorpionism, spider bites, pediculosis, and myiasis. Given the complex and diverse ecosystem of North Khorasan, implementing tailored and innovative strategies is essential for effective surveillance and early detection of arthropod-borne diseases, thus enabling timely and efficient management of these health threats.

Characterization of an Unusual Severe Yellow Fever Outbreak in the Colombian Andean Region.
BACKGROUND: Yellow fever (YF) reemerged in Colombia's Andean region during 2024-2025, outside the country's historically recognized endemic areas. We characterized critically ill adults admitted during this outbreak and described clinical features, organ dysfunction, supportive care, and in-hospital outcomes. METHODS: We conducted a prospective observational cohort study of consecutive adults with reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR)-confirmed YF admitted to the national referral intensive care unit in Ibagué, Tolima, Colombia, from March through September 2025. Clinical, laboratory, complication, intervention, and outcome data were prospectively captured using a standardized case report form. RESULTS: Sixty-one patients were analyzed; 22 died (36.1%). Non-survivors had lower platelet counts and fibrinogen and higher INR, aminotransferases, lactate dehydrogenase, and creatinine at ICU admission. Shock, acute kidney injury, acute respiratory distress syndrome, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and severe bleeding were more frequent among non-survivors. Prior YF vaccination was self-reported by 10 patients (16.4%). CONCLUSIONS: Severe YF in this Andean outbreak was characterized by hepatic-coagulation abnormalities and multisystem organ dysfunction. The occurrence of critical illness outside historically recognized endemic areas supports surveillance and vaccination strategies that can adapt to changing epidemiological risk.
